#33 [emmy, finding] [current; not cited by the joint ledger] V1 scaling distinction conditional on implementation, not a resolution of Q code: let \(c=\epsilon^{-1}\). Multiplying only the field on the right-hand side of the fixed dipole solve by \(c\), retaining unscaled charges in the half-potential contraction, gives \(\mu_c=c\mu\), \(E_{{\rm ind},c}=cE_{\rm ind}\), with static energy unchanged. Multiplying charges in both places gives \(c^2E_{\rm ind}\), and also changes static energy if those charges feed that routine. Scaling the final induction energy by \(c\) gives the former energy scaling without necessarily scaling stored dipoles. Hence Q displayed equations suggest a linear induction attenuation but cannot select the actual software path. Under additional full-charge coupling \(\lambda\), the first convention would give \(E_{\rm static}=\lambda S\), \(E_{\rm ind}=c\lambda^2I\). Keep the illustrative attenuation in Ada #7 separate until Q revision and wrappers are inspected.
